(Search snippet content — full article 403'd on direct fetch; CNN/CNBC/NPR own reporting language, cross-referenced)

CNN Business / CNBC / NPR, 7 August 2026 — US July 2026 jobs report:
- The US economy unexpectedly LOST 23,000 jobs in July, far below the forecast of an 80,000–83,000 gain, and well below the 34,000 average monthly gain of the prior 12 months.
- The BLS cut its May and June payroll estimates by a combined 103,000 jobs.
- Unemployment rate fell to 4.1% from 4.2% in June, but alongside a falling labour-force participation rate (61.4%, lowest in more than five years).
- Job losses concentrated: local government education −50,000, retail trade −19,000; health care +22,000.
- Average hourly earnings rose just 0.1% from June; annual wage growth slowed to 3.2% (five-year low), missing 3.5% expected.
- Fed implications: odds of a September rate move fell to 44% (from 57%); 58.3% for October.

Named analyst quotes (CNBC, "Wall Street reacts", 7 Aug 2026):
- Heather Long, chief economist, Navy Federal Credit Union: "This was a bleak report, and it signals the labor market is stalling again."
- Nicole Bachaud, labour economist, ZipRecruiter: "The July employment report solidified that the labor market is not out of the woods quite yet."
- Chris Zaccarelli, chief investment officer, Northlight Asset Management: the report is "a game changer" because "Before today, many were expecting that the Fed had no choice but to raise rates in order to fight stubbornly high inflation, because the job market was so strong, but this report shows that isn't the case."
NPR headline: "Employers unexpectedly cut 23,000 jobs in a sign of a wilting labor market."
